app/package.json:11 — typescript ^7.0.2, the stable native-port release (GA 2026-07-08; 7.1 still beta per github releases page)

latest_apis.rationale: Both toolchain deps are exactly the current stable releases (verified against vite.dev/blog/announcing-vite8 and the TS 7.0 announcement), and the app uses zero deprecated or superseded Vite/TS patterns; config injection is done the forward-compatible way.

app/src/main.ts:65-77,97 — history pushState/replaceState and history.scrollRestoration
app/src/pages/home.ts:26-43 — URL + searchParams for all filter state; parseInt + Number.isFinite for page parsing
app/src/main.ts:44 — main.replaceChildren()
app/src/components.ts:12-20 — loading='lazy' with explicit width/height for CLS
app/src/styles.css:193-195 — CSS Grid auto-fill/minmax; custom properties from tokens.css
app/server.mjs:23-55 — hand-rolled node:http static server with immutable asset caching instead of a serve framework

platform.rationale: Consistently platform-first across fetching, history, DOM, images, and CSS; the only miss is using render tokens where AbortController/AbortSignal would also cancel the in-flight requests, not just discard their results.

evidence: app/package.json:10-13 — only two devDependencies (vite, typescript), zero runtime dependencies
app/src/dom.ts:7 — 30-line typed createElement helper instead of a runtime DOM library
app/src/main.ts:15-22 — regex router instead of a routing package
app/package-lock.json — no transitive runtime deps; only Rolldown/oxc build toolchain
dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: routing, DOM building, debouncing, and serving are all done on native APIs, and the two dev deps are the current stable releases of their tools.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:117-125 — all HTTP behind one get<T>() with types at the boundary (interfaces at :18-104)
app/src/api.ts:129-133 — idFromUrl/isAlternateForm centralize the URL-shape and >10000 assumptions
app/src/pages/home.ts:8 — PAGE_SIZE in one place
app/src/main.ts:15-22 vs app/server.mjs:32 — route list duplicated between client router and server allow-list
app/server.mjs:14 vs app/src/api.ts:13 — API base URL default stated in two files
app/index.html:6 + app/server.mjs:26 — <!--app-config--> marker is a documented-in-comment contract between server and build output
churn_resistance.rationale: Upgrading Vite or TS would touch nothing here; data access is fully centralized and typed. Deducted for the client/server route duplication and the duplicated API base default — each new route or env change touches two files.

findings.issue: Server route allow-list (ROUTES) duplicates the client router's regexes in app/src/main.ts:15; a new route added only to the client serves index.html with a 404 status.
findings.suggestion: Share a single route-pattern module between server.mjs and main.ts, or derive the server allow-list from it.

findings.issue: Stale async renders are handled by token counters instead of AbortController, so in-flight fetches (e.g. move-table rebuilds on game switch) are never cancelled.
findings.suggestion: Thread an AbortSignal through get() and abort on re-render/re-selection; keep the token guard as a backstop.

findings.issue: The API base default 'http://localhost:9000' is duplicated in app/server.mjs:14; the two defaults can drift.
findings.suggestion: Have the client require window.__API_BASE_URL__ (fall back to a same-origin constant) so only the server owns the default.

findings.issue: idFromUrl extracts entity IDs by regex from API-provided URLs, coupling the app to PokeAPI's URL shape.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable given the documented API, but keep it the single extraction point (it is) and document the invariant; consider having the server config expose the id range assumptions instead of the literal 10000.

findings.issue: target ES2022 with lib ES2023 is a minor inconsistency (needless downleveling of a 2026 baseline).
findings.suggestion: Align target to ES2023+ (Vite 8's baseline already supports it).

summary: A lean, current-generation vanilla TS app: Vite 8.3 (Rolldown) and TypeScript 7.0.2 are exactly today's stable releases, runtime dependencies are zero, and every layer from fetching to routing to serving is built on first-party platform APIs. The architecture centralizes data access and types at the boundary, so framework or toolchain upgrades would touch almost nothing. Remaining churn risk is small and local: duplicated route definitions between client and server, a duplicated API base default, and missing AbortController cancellation behind the render-token guards.
